title: Concerning the Catechumen who found fault with the Elect: why he is angry.
text:
⟨p.219⟩
That one(?)
— Concerning the catechumen who has lived
He made complaint to the Elect, saying: "What is the matter with you? {0}
Once again it happened at a time, a catechumen stood
fast before Pakhaios the apostle. He said to him,
saying: 'The time which is good for a righteous one to be released — to be in gall, to fi-
ght with his fellow, casting his (own) release likewise into [{1}
two], in sayings, being divided, not yielding inward toward [their
ho]ur, that very (hour) which is good for them, while fighting with one another {3}
{4} other signs {5} upward; necessarily they are not righteous ones, the others
n {6} e who habitually {7} of these — necessarily they do not stand fast in the truth
of {8} reproof against them. Yet still I again make complaint, sa{9}ying
it, saying: "If indeed these are righteous ones, on what account do they
release? On what account are works in which they fight, themselves with one another, that
(it be) that one shall harm another, when they have nothing there in the cos-
mos for the sake of which they stand fast in him?"
Then sa{10}id the Illuminator to that catechumen th{11}ere: "A

{4}, the time when they shall be disturbed, and become wroth, and become choleric,
{5} bitter to one another — but you, do not be disturbed in your
heart at all, knowing rather that they stand fast in a bo-
-dy that is not theirs, being kneaded into the flesh of Sin which al{6}-
-so dwells in a strange land. Because of this they habitually become wroth them-
selv{7} and speak and proclaim hard words
into the face of one another. But the moment that you see them
wrothful, haughty-of-heart, do not be of two hearts toward them, do not
despise them, do not turn them away out of your heart,
nor set yourself up against them, do not say 'why also them-
-selves are they wroth, so that contention shall come to be {8} to them with
one a{9}nother?' Since you have known the mystery of the two
{10}two substances, you have learned that {11} and the evil dwell in
every man; you have learned also that the holy ones bear under a great
burden upon their shoulders. You then, in as much as you have known
all these things, it is {12} fitting to send forth words after the manner of (against)
the holy one — since you yourself al{13} have known that they bear up under
a great burden, they stand fa{14} the body which is not theirs.
 
Know also concerning {15} this other one in this manner: 'You stand
fast in Sin at all times; you do your life in the eat-
-ing and the drinking, in the desire of women, gold and
silver, your hands are loosed forth at all times to do violence to the Cro-
-ss of the Light. Behold, you stand fast in all these
sins, the holy ones are filled (with grief) on your account, you doing them; nevertheless
they do not deride them, nor do they hate you, nor do they distance
themselves from you, nor do they say, 'in as much as he sins, in this manner
there shall not come to him any teacher.' But rather they habitually keep silen{17}
in love and in sweetness-of-heart they habitually speak {18}
in the Wisdom of God, giving teaching to you, that you may {19}

that they are sins; and they do for you the mercies
all; they say to you, 'You are our brother, you
are our yokefellow who shall fight together with us for the Land
of Light.'
Behold then, you see how great the love
which they show inwardly toward you. They bear with you as a companion.
You yourself also — this is what proclaims to you, that you should love them{0}
and honor them. Do not at all despise them. The matter
is so that you may see no sins among them, they being firm of heart
with one another.
Then, when the Apostle had ut-
tered these words to that catechumen, he was persuaded
in his heart. He said to him, weeping: 'Forgive me'
'my sins, since I have known, my Lord, in truth concerning these
all that you have taught me about — namely, that the moment in which a
contention shall arise among the holy ones with one another, {2} hateful
not, since the Old Man also dwells in their {3}body
— because of this they habitually receive injury {4} of
they are stirred up against one another.'
